title: Group Alignment-Induced Sycophancy: A Two-Sided Evaluation of Steerable Pluralistic Alignment

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the intended gain in opinion match and unintended shifts in factual and social sycophancy when language models are aligned to Democrat versus Republican groups using stance alignment data.
Evaluating differences in opinion alignment gains and sycophancy metric shifts when language models are conditioned on Male versus Female demographic groups.
Assessing alignment performance and induced sycophantic behaviors when models are steered towards different education levels (high school or less, some college, college or above).
Comparing the impact of group alignment on opinion match and sycophancy profiles across low, middle, and high household income demographics.
Measuring disparities in alignment gains and sycophancy shifts when models are conditioned on married/partnered, previously married, or never married groups.
